target.title: fix(msteams): lowercase content type so attachment classification is case-insensitive
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`normalizeContentType` (`extensions/msteams/src/attachments/shared.ts`) only trimmed its input — it never lowercased. MIME types are **case-insensitive per RFC 2045**, and MS Teams relay payloads (SharePoint, OneDrive, Bot Framework CDN) routinely emit mixed-case values such as `"Image/PNG"` or `"Application/Vnd.Microsoft.Teams.File.Download.Info"`.

Every downstream comparison in the attachments module assumes a **lowercased** value:
- `isLikelyImageAttachment`: `contentType.startsWith("image/")` (shared.ts:241)
- `isDownloadableAttachment`: `contentType === "application/vnd.microsoft.teams.file.download.info"` (shared.ts:274)
- `isHtmlAttachment`: `contentType.startsWith("text/html")` (shared.ts:291)
- `html.ts`: `startsWith("text/html")`, `startsWith("application/vnd.microsoft.card.")` (lines 119-120, 177)
- `download.ts`: `contentType === "application/vnd.microsoft.teams.file.download.info"` (line 42)

So a mixed-case inbound attachment was **silently misclassified**: an image became a document, an HTML body was skipped, and a Teams file-download-info attachment was not resolved for download.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **Root cause:** `normalizeContentType` returned the trimmed-but-original-casing string, while all consumers compare against lowercase literals.
- **Fix:** Lowercase in `normalizeContentType` (`value.trim().toLowerCase()`). MIME types are case-insensitive by spec, so lowercasing can never turn a previously-matching value into a non-match — it only adds matches. One change fixes all six call sites at once.
- The sibling `inferPlaceholder` in the **same file** (shared.ts:228) already lowercases via `normalizeLowercaseStringOrEmpty`; this aligns the two code paths. The canonical repo helper `normalizeMimeType` (`packages/media-core/src/mime.ts`) also lowercases.

## User Impact

Inbound MS Teams attachments with mixed-case `contentType` are now classified correctly: images are recognized as images (inline/display + download routing), HTML attachment bodies are extracted, and Teams file-download-info attachments resolve their download URL. Lowercase `contentType` values are unaffected. No behavior change for non-Teams code paths.

## Linked context

N/A (no existing issue).

## Evidence

Reproduced with a `node` runtime script importing `normalizeContentType`, `isLikelyImageAttachment`, and `isDownloadableAttachment` to verify mixed-case MIME handling.

Terminal output of `node --import tsx /tmp/verify-msteams-content-type.mjs` after the fix:

```
[PASS] normalizeContentType("Image/PNG") = "image/png"
[PASS] normalizeContentType("Application/Vnd.Microsoft.Teams.File.Download.Info") = "application/vnd.microsoft.teams.file.download.info"
[PASS] isLikelyImageAttachment("Image/PNG", no ext) = true (matches lowercase true)
[PASS] isDownloadableAttachment(mixed-case download.info) = true (matches lowercase true)
[PASS] application/pdf is not an image (regression)
[PASS] undefined input -> undefined
[PASS] whitespace-only -> undefined
```

Before the fix, an inbound attachment with `contentType: "Image/PNG"` and no filename-extension hint was misclassified as a non-image, and the mixed-case Teams download-info `===` check missed its branch. After the fix, mixed-case types classify identically to their lowercase forms; non-image types still rejected; undefined/whitespace still return `undefined`.

## Real behavior proof

| # | Field | Value |
|---|-------|-------|
| 1 | Behavior or issue addressed | `normalizeContentType` did not lowercase, so `isLikelyImageAttachment({ contentType: "Image/PNG", name: "download" })` returned `false` (no filename-extension rescue) and the Teams download-info `===` check missed mixed-case types. |
| 2 | Real environment tested | Linux x64, Node 22, commit `caede8a4a91d2ce3c72bdd837cb8af0e5f5aceb0` |
| 3 | Exact steps or command run | `node --import tsx /tmp/verify-msteams-content-type.mjs` — imports `normalizeContentType`, `isLikelyImageAttachment`, `isDownloadableAttachment` and checks mixed-case image/download-info recognition plus ASCII/undefined/whitespace regressions. |
| 4 | Evidence after fix | Terminal capture of `node` runtime verification (copied live output):
```
[PASS] normalizeContentType("Image/PNG") = "image/png"
[PASS] normalizeContentType("Application/Vnd.Microsoft.Teams.File.Download.Info") = "application/vnd.microsoft.teams.file.download.info"
[PASS] isLikelyImageAttachment("Image/PNG", no ext) = true (matches lowercase true)
[PASS] isDownloadableAttachment(mixed-case download.info) = true (matches lowercase true)
[PASS] application/pdf is not an image (regression)
[PASS] undefined input -> undefined
[PASS] whitespace-only -> undefined
``` |
| 5 | Observed result after fix | Mixed-case `contentType` values are lowercased, so image/HTML/download-info attachments are now classified identically to their lowercase forms. Non-image types still rejected; undefined/empty/whitespace still return `undefined`. |
| 6 | What was not tested | Live Teams tenant traffic with a real mixed-case relay payload (no credentialled tenant here); the colocated unit tests cover `normalizeContentType`, `isLikelyImageAttachment`, and `isDownloadableAttachment` directly across mixed-case/lowercase/regression cases. |

## Tests and validation

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/msteams/src/attachments/
✓ shared.test.ts (63 tests)
✓ bot-framework.test.ts (21 tests)
✓ graph.test.ts (13 tests)
✓ remote-media.test.ts (5 tests)
Test Files  4 passed (4)
     Tests  102 passed (102)
```

New tests cover: `normalizeContentType` lowercasing/trimming/undefined handling, `isLikelyImageAttachment` mixed-case recognition + non-image regression, `isDownloadableAttachment` mixed-case download-info recognition.

## Risk checklist

- [x] One concern, one PR — only `normalizeContentType` lowercasing in the msteams attachments module.
- [x] No config/env/default surface change.
- [x] No SDK/protocol/auth/provider behavior change (local extension helper).
- [x] Backward compatible — lowercase inputs produce identical results; MIME types are case-insensitive by spec so lowercasing only adds matches, never removes one.
- [x] No new deps.
- [x] No CHANGELOG edit (per release policy).
- [x] Tests added.

- [x] Allow edits by maintainers
